title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection and hysteresis for rollout guards
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Improves automatic detection of latency/throughput regressions in the perf canary, adds hysteresis and configurable rollout guard knobs to reduce false positives during transient spikes. Backwards-compatible config defaults retained.
description:
Background: Canary-based detection currently has a relatively aggressive threshold and no hysteresis which causes noisy rollouts on transient load or garbage-collected tail latency spikes. This change introduces a multi-window detection algorithm, configurable hysteresis, and a small state-machine for rollout guard decisions so that canaries only block rollouts for sustained regressions.

What this PR does: Adds an enhanced detector that computes signal over short/medium/long windows (100ms, 1s, 30s by default), implements hysteresis that requires the primary metric to exceed threshold for N intervals and then to fall below a secondary threshold for M intervals before clearing, and plumbs these controls into the existing rollout_guards engine. Also:
- Adds feature flags and node-level config to tune windows/hysteresis for Dedicated/private deployments.
- Adds synthetic workload e2e to perf-canary harness to validate detection logic under controlled spikes.
- Improves metric instrumentation (adds canary.detector.windowed_p95, canary.detector.state transitions) so Console dashboards can show detector state.
- Adds unit and integration tests and CI gating; fixes a flaky test in perf-canary that caused false failures.

Design notes: The detector is implemented as a small rolling-window aggregator (circular buffers) to avoid allocations and to be cheap on the hot path; decisions are kept in a minimal state-machine (OK -> WARNING -> BLOCKED -> OK) with configurable timers. Default hysteresis values aim to keep sensitivity similar to prior behavior but reduce noise. See inline comments for rationale.

Testing: Unit tests cover window aggregation, hysteresis logic, and state transitions. Integration tests run a synthetic spike generator in the perf-canary harness and assert that a 5s spike does not block rollout but a 45s sustained regression does. CI initially failed due to a flaky test (perf_canary/test_spike_generator.py::test_spike_noise) which I fixed by stabilizing timing assertions and switching to mocked time in that test. All checks passed on final run.

Migration and rollout: Backwards compatible; defaults match previous sensitivity. Operators can opt into stricter behavior via the new canary.detector config block. No model or public API changes.

Related: ENG-2439 (canary tuning), SRE-112 (reduce false-positive rollbacks), SUP-3241 (customer incident that motivated hysteresis).

review_comments: Priya Nair: Overall this looks good. Can you add a short blurb in docs explaining hysteresis knobs and recommended defaults for Dedicated customers?

Avery Chen: Good catch — fixed boundary logic and added unit test to cover wrap-around edge-case.

Avery Chen: Confirmed fix uses mocked time and added a test with deterministic ticks. I opened a separate backport PR against release/2026-02 (will link after merge).
